method: Records independently phrased structural observations from pinned first-party release notes and companion known-issue pages. No source prose is copied.
selection: The release notes are maintained in the project's official repository and pinned to a reproducible commit and Git blob.
The sources represent different organizations and project types rather than one foundation or release tool.
Only reusable document structure is retained; project-specific wording, change lists, and contributor data remain upstream.

use_for: urgent upgrade notes before ordinary changes

sources.project_type: network transfer library and command-line tool
use_for: separation of changes, fixes, known bugs, and planned removals
routing detailed history to maintained references
avoid: project statistics without a reader decision

use_for: support and runtime compatibility before features
major and minor features by subsystem
avoid: examples unrelated to an upgrade decision

use_for: compatibility notes separated from new capabilities
avoid: internal changes in an end-user summary

sources.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later; some repository files use other licenses
use_for: future removals distinct from current behavior
known issues separated from release changes
verified workaround and upstream issue routing
avoid: long diagnostic transcripts when a stable error identifier exists

patterns.use_when: Opening a release announcement or release-notes document
patterns.shape: Identify the project and version, then state the release scope or support status needed to interpret the changes.

patterns.use_when: A release changes compatibility, support, configuration, or required operator action
patterns.shape: Place the affected scope, incompatible behavior, and verified upgrade action before general features.

patterns.use_when: A release has enough independent changes to require sections
patterns.shape: Group changes by reader decision, change kind, or stable subsystem; do not reproduce commit chronology.

patterns.use_when: Summarizing one user-visible feature, correction, or compatibility change
patterns.shape: Name the affected component and observable behavior in one entry; retain an issue or pull-request link only for traceability.

patterns.use_when: A feature is deprecated, scheduled for removal, or already incompatible
patterns.shape: Distinguish current behavior from future removal and state the affected scope, replacement, and removal version or date only when verified.

patterns.use_when: A release has unresolved limitations or a maintained external issue list
patterns.shape: Separate unresolved limitations from completed fixes, state the affected scope, and link the maintained issue source instead of copying its complete history.
